page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1.7xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor providing 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The instance features an x86_64 architecture with 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 33 MB shared L3 cache. It incorporates instruction extensions including AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, ADX, and FMA. System memory totals 64.0 GB RAM, adhering to a 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated GPUs or local storage, relying on external network-attached volumes, and delivers a baseline network throughput of 6 Gbps.

Benchmark measurements indicate a pronounced contrast between single-threaded and parallel processing capabilities. Single-core evaluations place the instance in lower tiers, recording 1109.99 on stress-ng and 960.0 on Geekbench, with single-threaded compression tests demonstrating reduced efficiency. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics perform consistently within the middle 50% tier, achieving a stress-ng score of 23557.71, a Geekbench multi-core score of 8426.0, and a PassMark CPU score of 22982.48. In targeted tasks, software compilation on Clang reached 18724.0, while PassMark database operations scored 8482.33.

Memory subsystem benchmarks show broad-spectrum throughput with 1313.24 GB/sec for small cached reads, descending to 74.54 GB/sec read and 34.35 GB/sec write for large 256 MB blocks, accompanied by a PassMark memory score of 1809.96. Static web serving throughput reached 13.68 GB/sec, alongside 23.27 million operations per second in Redis SET operations. Text generation benchmarks for small language models show moderate latency limitations, generating 72.38 tokens per second on a 135M model and 10.19 tokens per second on a 7B model.

From an engineering perspective, resource density favors horizontally threaded or distributed computing profiles over high single-thread clock demands. The absence of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs defines its primary focus on compute throughput over direct I/O density. The ecs.sn1.7xlarge is suitable for batch processing pipelines, multi-threaded Clang compilation, middle-tier web serving pools, and multi-core application services.

Configured with 64.0 GB of memory, it provides a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides no integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators, routing all system I/O through a 6 Gbps baseline network connection. Performance testing highlights modest single-core throughput, balanced by solid multi-core execution across stress-ng, Geekbench, and PassMark tests. With 23.27 million Redis SET operations per second and steady multi-threaded compilation capabilities, it serves distributed computing environments, batch ETL jobs, multi-threaded backend services, and web application serving tiers.
